newsitem.title: USA: SEC alleges insider trades in Pechiney case.
newsitem.headline: SEC alleges insider trades in Pechiney case.

text.p: The U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission said Monday that two individuals agreed to settle the agency's charges of insider trading in connection with the 1988 takeover of Triangle Industries Inc by France's Pechiney SA

The SEC complaint, which seeks the forfeiture of about $6.5 million in allegedly illegal trading profits related to the so-called "Pechiney affair", also names five other foreign nationals and two foreign firms.
The two defendants who agreed to settle charges, Lebanese businessman Samir Traboulsi and Patrick Gruman, did so without admitting or denying the allegations, the SEC said.

All of the individual defendants in the SEC case were convicted in France for their involvement in the high-profile insider trading case, part of a spate of scandals contributing to the Socialists' general election defeat in 1993.
Triangle was the parent company of U.S.-based American Can.

To settle the SEC case, Traboulsi agreed to pay $250,000, which the SEC said represents part of the proceeds of the Triangle trades made by individuals he allegedly alerted to the pending takeover. The SEC said it waived financial penalties for Gruman because of his inability to pay.
The SEC said its action also involves the forfeiture of about $1.1 million in profits in prejudgment interest realized on certain trades by the late Roger-Patrice Pelat.
The agency said it is still pursuing its case against the other defendants.
